# Rust Decisions

What rustfmt decides, so a reviewer does not.

## Format

One tool decides the layout of a file, so a reviewer does not.

| id | title | check | fix | requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`rust/formatted`](#a-rust-file-is-as-rustfmt-writes-it) | A Rust file is as rustfmt writes it | error · command | safe |  |

### A Rust file is as rustfmt writes it

`rust/formatted` · project · error · command · fix: safe

*Vertical and horizontal openness, indentation and the placement of braces are team rules, and a team keeps them by letting one tool decide, not by reviewing them (Martin, Clean Code ch. 5 Team rules). The check is the tool's own list mode: one finding per file it would change, at line 1, that names the file. The fix is the tool as a filter, which writes the file as it formats it; it has the lowest priority, so the fix of any other decision wins an overlap and the formatting follows it as a safe follow-up of the change. The check is run once over the project because rustfmt formats the files a `mod` declares along with the file it is given, so what it finds in one file depends on others. rustfmt does not read `Cargo.toml`, and the edition decides what it accepts and how it writes some items, so both programs pass it the edition of the crate that holds the file: the nearest `Cargo.toml` that sets one, in its package or in the workspace it inherits from, else the latest. `cargo fmt` does the same, but it needs a manifest at the root of the project and cannot be a filter over one file. The programs are the bundled catalog's own, so they run in a project nobody trusted.*

A Rust file MUST equal the output of rustfmt.

Derived from: Martin, Clean Code (2008), G24 Follow Standard Conventions; Martin, Clean Code (2008), ch. 5 Vertical openness and density; Martin, Clean Code (2008), ch. 5 Horizontal openness and indentation; Martin, Clean Code (2008), ch. 5 Team rules; rustfmt: https://rust-lang.github.io/rustfmt/

```diff
--- a/src/lib.rs
+++ b/src/lib.rs
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
-pub fn run()->i32{1}
+pub fn run() -> i32 {
+    1
+}
```
